summary: The hypothesis that simulated annealing with grid-based nearest-neighbor construction would beat the 33.5 baseline was confirmed — the solution scored 69.5, roughly double the baseline. However, the score has plateaued: nearest-neighbor construction alone accounts for ~93% of the final score (64.5 of 69.5), and SA optimization with random swap/2-opt moves adds only ~5 points despite testing 12+ variants.
key_points: Score achieved: 69.5 vs. 33.5 baseline probe — a clear improvement, confirming the directional prediction.
Nearest-neighbor construction alone scores 64.5; SA adds only ~5 points (~7% improvement), indicating random local moves are throughput-limited for N=200K within the 2-second time budget.
The carrot penalty (10% on every 10th step from non-prime cities) affects only ~1% of total cost; the prime-scheduling post-pass captures most available savings from this structure.
To break past 69.5, the next iteration should explore neighbor-list-guided 2-opt, Or-opt, or Lin-Kernighan style moves that make geometrically informed improvements rather than random perturbations.
12 algorithm variants were tested and all converged to 69.5 ± 0.5, suggesting the current approach has been fully exploited.
